precepts.text: Priests not found in the register were put from the priesthood as polluted, and were not to eat of the most holy things till there stood up a priest with Urim and Thummim.
precepts.point: Joshua likewise was to stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord; the Most High gave revelation through it.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
The significance of the Urim and Thummim shows in Nehemiah's day. Of the priests, the children of Habaiah, the children of Koz and the children of Barzillai “sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but it was not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood.”

“And the Tirshatha said unto them, that they should not eat of the most holy things, till there stood up a priest with Urim and Thummim.” The Tirshatha is Nehemiah the governor. Determining that lineage was outside human ability, so it waited on the priest with the divine discerner, by which the high priest ascertained the will of the Most High in important matters affecting the nation. That is the judgment of the children of Israel that Aaron bore upon his heart before the Lord.

points: When the wall was built and the doors set up, Nehemiah appoints the porters, the singers, and the Levites, and sets his brother Hanani and Hananiah the ruler of the palace over Jerusalem.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: The city was large and great, but the people within it were few and the houses not yet built.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: The Most High puts it into Nehemiah's heart to gather the nobles, rulers, and people to be reckoned by genealogy, and he finds the register of those who came up first.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: This register matches the one recorded in Ezra 2. Every name means something, and Israel kept a careful record of exactly who returned to the land.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: The priests, the Levites, the singers, the porters, the Nethinims, and the children of Solomon's servants are all counted by their houses.

The Nethinims were the temple servants, distinct from the Nephilim of Genesis. The two words sound alike but are not the same, the Nethinims being those given to assist in the service of the house of the Most High.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: Some came up from Telmelah, Telharsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer but could not show their father's house or their seed, whether they were of Israel.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: The priests who could not find their register by genealogy were put from the priesthood as polluted. The Tirshatha forbade them the most holy things until a priest stood up with Urim and Thummim, because a man had to prove he came from the line of Aaron.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: The whole congregation together numbered forty and two thousand three hundred and threescore, beside their menservants and maidservants.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: Among them were singing men and singing women, and their horses, mules, camels, and asses are all counted. There is nothing wrong with a brother singing, and if the Most High gives the gift, it should be used.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: Some of the chief of the fathers give to the work: gold, silver, priests' garments, and offerings to the treasure.

note.label: Nehemiah 7: The Register of Those Who Came Up First

points: So the priests, the Levites, the porters, the singers, the Nethinims, and all Israel dwell in their cities, setting back in order the things that had been lacking.
